test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 23 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
A spherical mirror diverges a beam of light, which is incident on it. Which of the following statement(s) about the mirror is/are true?

i)The mirror used is convex.

ii) The mirror has positive focal length.

iii) The image formed by this mirror can be seen on a screen.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (i) and (ii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A spherical mirror that diverges a beam of light is known as a convex mirror.
 
• Convex mirrors have a positive focal length, which means the focal point is behind the mirror.
 
• Convex mirrors form virtual images, which cannot be projected on a screen.
 
• These mirrors are commonly used in applications where a wide field of view is needed, such as in vehicle rearview mirrors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convex Mirror**

 
 
• A convex mirror is a spherical mirror where the reflective surface bulges outward.
 
• They are also known as diverging mirrors because they spread out light rays that have been reflected.
 
• Convex mirrors always form virtual, erect, and diminished images.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length**
 
 
• Focal length is the distance between the mirror's surface and the focal point.
 
• For convex mirrors, the focal length is positive.
 
• The focal point is the point where parallel light rays either converge or appear to diverge after reflecting off the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Virtual Image**
 
 
• A virtual image is an image that cannot be obtained on a screen.
 
• Virtual images are formed when light rays appear to meet at a point behind the mirror.
 
• Convex mirrors always produce virtual images.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Convex Mirrors**
 
 
• Used in vehicle rearview mirrors to provide a wider field of view.
 
• Installed in hallways and stores for security purposes to monitor a larger area.
 
• Utilized in optical instruments like telescopes to direct light.
